transcript: Something I learned recently... I've been working on negotiation, mainly because I noticed I give discounts too fast. Like, a client pushes a little and I just say, okay, ten percent off. So a colleague recommended a book, Never Split the Difference, and I read it over maybe a month, on the bus mostly. The main thing I took from it is asking more questions instead of answering the price objection straight away. Like, what does the budget look like, what happens if you don't solve this. I've tried it in a few calls since then. It helps, clients talk more, and a couple of times I didn't need to discount at all. I haven't really measured it though, I should probably look at my average discount before and after, that would be interesting. I also watched some role-play videos on YouTube but they were a bit cheesy. My plan is to practise with my team lead, she's very good at it, maybe once a week if she has time. So yeah, negotiation, and I'm still learning it, I'm not great yet but I'm better than before.
